papers.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Risk Prediction after Total Hip Replacement at Kandou Hospital
papers.abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a clinically significant complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA), requiring a clear distinction between observed postoperative events and model-based risk estimates. This prospective cohort study enrolled 62 patients who underwent THA at Prof. Dr. R. D. Kandou Hospital in Manado, Indonesia, between January 2023 and December 2024, with a 90-day follow-up period. Clinical characteristics, Wells scores, D-dimer levels, fibrinogen levels, and Doppler ultrasonography findings were recorded. Descriptive findings indicated that 46 participants (74%) were male, 48 (77%) had elevated D-dimer levels, and all documented Doppler ultrasonography examinations yielded normal findings. A Monte Carlo simulation comprising 10,000 iterations was also performed using a logistic regression equation with coefficients reportedly derived from published literature rather than estimated from the study cohort. The simulation yielded a median predicted DVT prevalence of 7.3%, with a 95% prediction interval of 0%–29%. However, this estimate represented a simulation-derived outcome rather than the observed incidence of postoperative DVT. The available manuscript did not report the actual number of incident DVT events during the 90-day follow-up and contained an unresolved inconsistency between the exclusion of patients with active cancer and the reported inclusion of seven participants with active cancer. [AUTHOR DATA REQUIRED: Confirm the number of observed DVT events during follow-up and clarify the eligibility criteria concerning active cancer.] Overall, the study provided descriptive information on clinical characteristics and potential DVT risk factors in a local THA population, alongside an exploratory simulation-based risk estimation framework. Nevertheless, cohort-specific predictive associations, model discrimination, and calibration could not be established without verification of the observed clinical outcomes, model coefficients, and estimation procedures.

papers.title: Experimental Study and Physics-Informed Machine Learning on Sustainable Concrete Using Sugarcane Bagasse Ash and Distilled Sewage Water
papers.abstract: The increasing environmental burden associated with cement production and freshwater consumption has created a need for sustainable alternatives in concrete production. This study investigates the combined utilization of Sugarcane Bagasse Ash (SCBA) as a partial cement replacement and Distilled SewageWater (DSW) as an alternative mixing-water source in M25–grade concrete. Seven concrete mixtures (M0–M6) were prepared by incorporating 0–30% SCBA and 0–40% DSW while maintaining a constant binder content of 400 kg/m3 and water-to-binder ratio of 0.50. Compressive strength was experimentally evaluated after 7, 14, and 28 days of curing. The results demonstrated that moderate replacement levels improved strength, with the mixture containing 10% SCBA and 20% DSW achieving the highest compressive strengths of 20.8, 26.1, and 34.2 MPa at 7, 14, and 28 days, respectively. The improvement was attributed to the pozzolanic activity and micro-filler effect of SCBA, together with adequate water availability. Higher replacement levels resulted in strength reduction because of cement dilution and reduced calcium hydroxide availability. Furthermore, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) models were developed to predict compressive strength using key mix–design parameters and curing age. Both models exhibited excellent predictive performance, with R2 values exceeding 0.999 during the evaluated stages. ANN provided slightly higher numerical accuracy, whereas PINN demonstrated more consistent validation and testing behaviour, indicating improved generalisation and physical consistency. The findings demonstrate that the integrated experimental, physics-informed modelling, and explainable–AI framework can support the development and optimization of sustainable SCBA–DSW concrete while reducing dependence on conventional cement and freshwater resources.

papers.title: Finite element model updating of building structures under seismic excitation: A parallelized latent space-based Bayesian framework
papers.abstract: Enhancing seismic fragility and risk assessment of nuclear power plants relies on accurate prediction of reactor building responses to seismic hazards, which can be further improved through dynamic analysis of high-fidelity finite element (FE) models. However, FE models often exhibit non-negligible discrepancies from actual structures due to various sources of uncertainty, necessitating FE model updating with rigorous quantification of associated uncertainties. This paper presents a GPU-accelerated latent space-based Bayesian framework for FE model updating of building structures. In the proposed framework, high-dimensional structural response data (e.g., time histories or frequency response functions) are projected into a low-dimensional latent space using a multimodal variational autoencoder (MVAE), thereby enabling efficient and tractable likelihood evaluation without explicit modeling in the original observation space. Once trained, the surrogate enables amortized inference, allowing posterior sampling to be performed without additional simulator evaluations. We specifically employ a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) sampler, whose population-based formulation allows parallel evaluation of the approximate likelihood on GPUs, resulting in computational efficiency and robustness against multimodal and complex posterior distributions. The proposed framework is evaluated through numerical benchmarking using a shear-type building structure with a multimodal posterior distribution. The results indicate that the proposed approach can recover the major posterior modes while achieving efficient inference through GPU-based parallel evaluation. We further apply the framework to experimental data from a shaking table test of a reinforced concrete building structure. The results suggest that the inferred posterior distributions and posterior predictive responses are consistent with the observed data, even in the presence of sparse observations that induce complex posterior distributions.

papers.title: Endogenous protein adsorption and functional presentation at bone-regenerative biointerfaces
papers.abstract: Bone-regenerative materials rapidly acquire proteins from blood, marrow fluid, and the surrounding tissue. The resulting interface depends on protein quantity, identity, orientation, conformation, and exchange, rather than total adsorption alone. This narrative critical review examines selected mechanisms through which these features influence receptor recognition and responses relevant to bone repair. We use the descriptive term interfacial protein state and propose a joint reporting profile for comparisons made under matched exposure and sampling conditions. Primary evidence is distinguished by protein source, experimental setting, causal perturbation, and limits of interpretation. The strongest mechanistic examples concern fibronectin presentation and integrin signaling, selected fibrinogen-dependent inflammatory pathways, and material-assisted presentation of exogenous growth factors. Quantitative examples of surface density, accessibility, dissociation, and retained BMP-2 dose are reported with their experimental conditions. Autologous platelet-rich plasma and platelet-rich fibrin are considered as clinically relevant precoatings whose preparation and release behavior require separate characterization. Competition between host cells and bacteria for the conditioned interface is also addressed. Hemostatic-inflammatory, angiogenic-matrix-forming, and mineralization-remodeling processes are presented as overlapping biological contexts, not as a validated schedule for programming protein exchange. Evidence from purified coatings and dispersed nanoparticles is not treated as proof of endogenous recruitment or clinical bone healing. Predicting outcomes across materials, guiding patient-specific implant selection, and replacing growth-factor delivery through endogenous capture remain unvalidated. The proposed measurements organize causal tests and identify evidence gaps; they do not define a universal protein-state score or an established clinical design rule.

papers.title: Process-informed micromechanical modelling of anisotropy and defect sensitivity in additively manufactured 316L stainless steel
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) of 316L stainless steel produces melt-pool-driven columnar grain structures that result in significant mechanical anisotropy. This study develops a predictive, process-informed 3D geometrically based process-structure (GBPS) framework integrated with crystal plasticity finite element (CPFE) modelling to simulate the tensile response of AM 316L. The framework replaces the need for experimental microstructure data with an idealised, computationally efficient 3D unit cell. Methodological optimisations, including the use of cuboid elements and regularised grain boundaries, achieve a 10-fold reduction in CPU time with negligible (<1%) loss in accuracy. The model successfully predicts the characteristic anisotropy of AM 316L, yielding ≈9% higher yield strength and ≈12% higher UTS in the transverse direction compared to the build direction. Furthermore, a defect-sensitivity study reveals that horizontal build orientations are significantly more susceptible to porosity-induced strain localisation, showing a ≈15% drop in ductility at 2% porosity. This framework provides a physically motivated yet lean tool for exploring process-structure–property relationships in PBF-LB alloys across varied scanning strategies.

papers.title: Influence of constitutive model parameter uncertainty on fragility estimates: Application to a Chilean highway bridge
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification and propagation are central components of Performance-Based Earthquake Engineering (PBEE). Although seismic hazard is widely recognized as a dominant source of variability in structural response, comparatively less attention has been paid to how constitutive model parameter uncertainty propagates through demand, capacity, and limit-state definitions to the fragility of individual structures. This work investigates the propagation of constitutive model parameter uncertainty within the PBEE framework using a representative Chilean highway bridge as a case study. The study employs, nonlinear finite element modeling with uncertain constitutive parameters, and cloud fragility analysis with a suite of 211 unscaled ground motions selected following site-specific probabilistic seismic hazard analysis spanning return periods from 30 to 5000 years. Results show that constitutive parameter uncertainty, propagated through both structural demand and component capacity estimates, can substantially affect component fragility predictions. Extreme cases show a range between 20% and 90% probability of exceeding a certain limit state, at a given intensity. Finally, global sensitivity analysis is performed, leveraging efficient simulation with Gaussian process surrogate models to compute total Sobol indices. The surrogate models show a R 2 score over 0.9 for all components, while contributing less than 5.5% to the total variance in fragility estimates due to posterior uncertainty. These indices provide insight into the composition of uncertainty in fragility estimates in terms of the relative contribution of individual model parameters and their interactions. For the case-study bridge, only a small subset of parameters is found to dominate the induced uncertainty at higher intensity levels, with elastomeric bearings governing component interactions, thus offering guidance for prioritizing future experimental data collection campaigns.

papers.title: Anatomical Variations Encountered During the Posterior Approach to the Hip Joint
papers.abstract: The posterior approach to the hip joint remains widely used for primary total hip arthroplasty because it provides extensive exposure while preserving the abductor mechanism. Safe execution, however, depends on recognizing anatomical variation within the gluteal region. This narrative review synthesizes variations encountered sequentially during posterior hip exposure and organizes them into superficial, muscular, neurovascular, and osseous domains. Key considerations include branching patterns of the posterior femoral cutaneous and superior cluneal nerves, morphological variation in the short external rotators and quadratus femoris, variation in the sciatic nerve-piriformis relationship, persistent embryonic vessels, os acetabuli, and proximal femoral morphology. Accordingly, reported frequencies should be interpreted in light of study design and sample size. By arranging these findings according to surgical planes and distinguishing documented clinical complications from anatomy-based theoretical risks, this review provides a practical anatomical roadmap for preoperative planning and intraoperative orientation. The direct effect of many variants on surgical outcomes remains uncertain and warrants prospective clinical study.

papers.title: Simulation of different laser interaction modes on melt flow and heat transfer behavior during laser powder bed fusion process of IN718 alloy
papers.abstract: Among the numerous parameters of the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process, laser power, scanning speed, and laser spot diameter directly affect the melt pool size. In this work, a single-pass simulation of the LPBF process for IN718 alloy with different process parameters was carried out using computational fluid dynamics. Results show that laser spot diameter is the most important parameter affecting the depth-to-width ratio of the molten pool and the laser melting mode, followed by laser power, and finally scanning speed. An increase in laser spot diameter induces a transition in the laser melting mode from keyhole mode to conduction mode, passing through a transition mode. Heat transfer in the conduction mode is dominated by thermal conduction, whereas convection is the dominant heat transfer mechanism in the keyhole mode, with the transition mode in between. The flow field analysis shows that two vortices appear in the upper part of the melt pool cross-section in the conduction mode. This is significantly different from the keyhole mode, where vortices appear at the bottom of the melt pool. This difference in flow leads to differences in temperature distribution in the melt pool and therefore leads to different solidification microstructures, mainly in terms of equiaxed grain content. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for simpler and more practical process optimization in controlling solidification microstructures during the LPBF process.

papers.title: Assessment of the quality of visual life in patients using a personalized technique for corneal segment implantation based on a mathematical biomechanical model of the cornea
papers.abstract: Implantation of intrastromal corneal ring segments (ICRS) is considered one of the key surgical rehabilitation methods for patients with progressive keratoconus. Personalized selection of the configuration and placement of ICRS based on a mathematical biomechanical model potentially increases effectiveness and improves visual quality of life compared with the standard method. The aim of the study: To perform a comparative analysis of clinical and functional outcomes and visual quality of life in patients with keratoconus after standard versus personalized ICRS implantation, using a custom electronic questionnaire based on the NEI VFQ 25. Research methodology: The study included 204 patients (204 eyes) with progressive stage II–III keratoconus, randomized into two groups: personalized ICRS implantation based on a corneal “digital twin” (n = 92) and standard implantation according to the Keraring nomogram (n = 112). Uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), higher order aberrations (HOAs), and visual quality of life were assessed using a modified electronic NEI VFQ 25 questionnaire supplemented with questions about photic phenomena and neuroadaptation time. Follow up visits were carried out preoperatively and at 1, 6, 12, and 24 months. The results of the research: In both groups ICRS implantation led to significant improvement in UDVA and CDVA and to a reduction in HOAs; however, the improvement was more pronounced with the personalized approach (p 0.001). The total score on the modified NEI VFQ 25 increased significantly in both groups, but the gain and the scores on subscales for visual functioning, social functioning, adaptation to glare and halos, and neuroadaptation time were substantially higher in the study group (p 0.001). Strong positive correlations were found between functional measures and the composite quality of life score, and moderate inverse correlations between photic complaints and aberration parameters. Conclusion: Personalized ICRS implantation based on a corneal “digital twin” provides not only superior functional outcomes but also greater improvement in visual quality of life and tolerance of photic phenomena compared with the standard technique, supporting the advisability of implementing biomechanically guided planning in clinical practice.

papers.title: Advanced alginate engineering strategies toward next-generation precision orthopedics.
papers.abstract: The rising clinical demand for treating musculoskeletal defects necessitates viable alternatives to traditional bone grafting. Alginate, a naturally derived polysaccharide, has become a leading bioink for 3D bioprinting owing to its abundance, rapid ionic crosslinking, and scalable manufacturing. Yet, intrinsic drawbacks-poor cell adhesivity, unpredictable degradation kinetics, and overall low bioactivity-continue to impede clinical translation. Advances in chemical modification and mechanical reinforcement have begun to reprogram alginate into dynamic extracellular matrix mimics with enhanced osteogenic guidance. These structural modifications are further complemented by sophisticated fabrication techniques such as ion-exchange-mediated stiffness gradients, multi-material extrusion, and 4D printing. Concurrently, the design of next-generation bioinks is transitioning from passive scaffolding to active immunomodulation to drive endogenous regeneration. Yet, clinical translation remains constrained by critical challenges, notably ensuring long-term in vivo stability, matching scaffold degradation kinetics with de novo tissue formation, and navigating the complex manufacturing and regulatory requirements for combination products. By evaluating advanced alginate engineering strategies, with a specific focus on patient-specific, immunomodulatory, and dynamically adaptive grafts, as well as its emerging applications in organoid culture, this review serves as a valuable reference to guide the future development and clinical translation of next-generation alginate-based biomaterials.

papers.abstract: Modern prosthodontics is characterized by the rapid development of digital technologies that encompass virtually all stages of prosthetic treatment, from initial diagnosis to the fabrication and fixation of definitive prosthetic restorations. Despite the active implementation of digital technologies into clinical practice, the issue of comparative evaluation of conventional and digital impression techniques during implant-supported prosthetic treatment remains relevant. In this regard, the comparative clinical and functional assessment of the outcomes of prosthetic rehabilitation on dental implants using conventional and digital impression techniques represents an important scientific and practical task aimed at improving contemporary prosthetic rehabilitation protocols. Objective. To increase the effectiveness of prosthetic rehabilitation in patients with partial edentulism through the fabrication of implant-supported fixed prosthetic restorations. Materials and Methods. The study was conducted at the Department of Prosthetic Dentistry and the University Dental Center of Kharkiv National Medical University. A total of 48 patients aged 28 to 67 years with partial secondary edentulism who underwent prosthetic rehabilitation using dental implants were included in the study. All patients were divided into two clinical groups according to the implant system used. Ethical considerations were addressed in accordance with the legislation of Ukraine, Articles 7, 8, and 12 of the Law of Ukraine “On Medicinal Products” (1996), the principles of Good Clinical Practice (International Council for Harmonisation Good Clinical Practice, ICH GCP, 2008), Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 690 dated September 23, 2009, “On Approval of the Procedure for Conducting Clinical Trials of Medicinal Products and Expert Evaluation of Clinical Trial Materials and the Standard Regulations on Ethics Committees,” with amendments and additions, as well as the Declaration of Helsinki of the World Medical Association (1964, latest revision – 2024). The article is a fragment of the planned research project of the Department of Prosthetic Dentistry of Kharkiv National Medical University entitled “Integration of Modern Achievements in Medicine, Materials Science, and Technologies of Diagnosis, Treatment, and Rehabilitation of Patients in the Clinic of Prosthetic Dentistry” (State Registration No. 0125U000939, implementation period: 2025–2027; Principal Investigator – Head of the Department of Prosthetic Dentistry, Doctor of Medical Sciences, Professor I.V. Yanishen). All patients were in satisfactory general health and had no absolute contraindications to dental implantation and subsequent prosthetic treatment. After completion of osseointegration and maturation of peri-implant tissues, the prosthetic stage of treatment was performed. Within each clinical group, two impression protocols were applied: a conventional technique using an open-tray impression and A-silicone impression material, and a digital technique using an intraoral scanner and scan bodies. Follow-up examinations were performed at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after fixation of the prosthetic restorations. Statistical analysis was carried out using methods of descriptive and inferential statistics with determination of the mean value (M), standard deviation (SD), Student’s t-test, and the level of statistical significance at p < 0.05. Results A total of 106 dental implants were placed, including 52 Alfabio implants and 54 Megagen implants. The average number of implants per patient was 2.21 ± 0.8. During follow-up examinations at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, no cases of implant loss or impaired osseointegration were recorded, resulting in an implant survival rate of 100%. The obtained results are consistent with contemporary studies and confirm the high effectiveness of digital technologies in implant-supported prosthodontics. The use of intraoral scanners allows optimization of both clinical and laboratory stages of treatment, improves the accuracy of prosthetic restorations, and enhances patients’ quality of life. Conclusions. The use of digital intraoral scanning reduces the duration of the clinical impression-taking stage by 1.9 times compared with conventional A-silicone impression materials. Implant-supported fixed prosthetic restorations provide a statistically significant improvement in masticatory efficiency, as confirmed by functional assessment at all follow-up periods. Following prosthetic rehabilitation, patients demonstrated a substantial improvement in quality-of-life indicators according to the treatment satisfaction questionnaire.

papers.title: A digital twin-driven investigation of coupled vertical-torsional soft flutter of a flat closed-box bridge deck section
papers.abstract: Soft flutter or limit cycle flutter, a nonlinear self-limiting vibration phenomenon, has been observed in blunt-body cross sections of bridge decks in recent years. This study therefore proposes a digital twin approach to investigate coupled vertical-torsional soft flutter of a flat closed-box bridge deck section and explore its physical mechanisms. In the proposed approach, the coupled vertical-torsional soft flutter of a flat closed-box bridge deck section was first observed through wind tunnel tests utilising a synchronised force-vibration testing system and regarded as a physical entity, and the coupled vertical-torsional vibration responses and self-excited aerodynamic forces of the deck section were recorded. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation model, accounting for fluid-structure interaction and nonlinearities, was then constructed as a virtual entity of the physical entity. A Gaussian process surrogate model and a phased parameter optimisation strategy were then introduced to establish a self-learning digital twin to achieve high-precision inversion of mechanical damping ratio and stiffness of the deck section. Finally, a parameter-wind speed mapping covering the entire tested wind speed range was constructed, forming a digital twin system capable of predicting soft flutter responses at untested wind speeds. It is demonstrated that the established digital twin accurately reproduces the limit-cycle vibration characteristics of the coupled vertical-torsional soft flutter. The digital twin effectively reveals the intrinsic relationship between aerodynamic energy input, damping dissipation, and vibration stability, and provides an effective pathway for nonlinear soft flutter analysis and response prediction of blunt-body deck sections.

papers.title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces
papers.abstract: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. After training RNO on only the pre-tipping dynamics, we employ it to detect future tipping points using an uncertainty-based approach. In particular, we propose a conformal prediction framework to forecast tipping points by monitoring deviations from physics constraints (such as conserved quantities and partial differential equations), enabling forecasting of these abrupt changes along with a rigorous measure of uncertainty. We illustrate our proposed methodology on nonstationary ordinary and partial differential equations, such as the Lorenz-63 and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equations. We also apply our methods to forecast a climate tipping point in stratocumulus cloud cover and airfoil wake and stall transitions using only limited knowledge of the governing equations. For the latter, we show that our proposed method zero-shot generalizes to forecasting multiple future tipping points under varying Reynolds numbers. In our experiments, we demonstrate that even partial or approximate physics constraints can be used to accurately forecast future tipping points.

papers.title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
papers.abstract: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic “gatekeeper,” regulating oxidation through a “breathing mode” of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a “rupture mode” leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

papers.title: Spatial Statistics for Screening Molecular Structures
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The dominant paradigm in computational materials discovery relies on heavily parameterized deep architectures, including message‐passing graph and equivariant networks, that typically require large density functional theory (DFT)‐labeled training sets and produce nonconvex latent representations complicating inverse design, a limitation in the data‐scarce regimes common to exploratory screening. Standard formulations also face specific difficulties with chemically disordered configurations and with distinguishing chiral geometries (e.g., ‐invariant models are reflection‐blind by construction). These are task‐ and formulation‐dependent tendencies, not universal deficiencies, and are reduced by pre‐training, transfer, and equivariant designs. This review presents spatial‐statistics feature engineering as a physically rigorous, deployable complement. Molecular structures are encoded as voxelized fields, and two‐point auto‐ and cross‐correlations are evaluated deterministically via Fast Fourier Transforms, moving spatial pattern recognition into a closed‐form, physics‐informed operation. Principal component analysis yields low‐dimensional, convex representations supporting lean neural networks and non‐parametric surrogates, achieving sub‐2% normalized errors from as little as 0.1% of the dataset in reported cases. Demonstrated across periodic crystals, disordered high‐entropy alloys, and non‐periodic molecules, the framework enables Bayesian active learning and zero‐shot extrapolation on commodity hardware, which remains challenging for large‐scale architectures at equal data budgets.

papers.title: Metropolis-scale resilient and trustworthy traffic flow inference using multi-source data
papers.abstract: Inferring network-wide traffic states from sparse observations with high accuracy and trustworthy uncertainty quantification is essential for intelligent transportation systems, yet it remains challenging due to the underdetermined nature of the problem, multifaceted disturbances in sensing networks, and the inherent conflicts among multiple inference subtasks when modeled jointly. We propose the Task-Aware Attentive Neural Process (TA-ANP), a unified probabilistic framework for resilient and trustworthy global traffic state inference (GTSI) by fusing floating car data (FCD) with sparse fixed-detector measurements. By casting GTSI as a stochastic process, TA-ANP leverages the meta-learning properties of neural processes to adapt rapidly to changes in sensing configurations without retraining. A task-aware multi-query attention module with distinct spatiotemporal inductive biases is introduced to jointly handle three GTSI subtasks—real-time estimation at unobserved locations, forecasting at both observed and unobserved locations—while mitigating cross-task interference. For uncertainty quantification, we combine neural processes with Monte Carlo Dropout to capture both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. To support metropolis-scale evaluation, we construct the Metropolitan Multi-Source Traffic Dataset (MMTD), integrating fixed-loop sensor measurements, FCD statistics, and OpenStreetMap road-network data over an urban network of 26,166 road segments, including 2371 fixed-sensor-equipped segments used for quantitative evaluation. Experiments across multiple independently generated sensor configurations show that TA-ANP achieves best performance across all subtasks under deterministic and probabilistic metrics. The resulting well-calibrated uncertainties enable more efficient fixed-sensor placement with fewer sensor deployments. Under a Damage–Repair–Addition sensing lifecycle, TA-ANP demonstrates superior resilience in terms of disturbance absorption, performance recovery, and adaptability to unseen sensing configurations.The code and processed datasets are publicly available on GitHub and Zenodo , respectively.

papers.title: Polymer-Linked Nanoparticle Networks Running on Heat Can Act as Computing Devices
papers.abstract: Abstract Developing physical neural network (PNN) hardwares is important to next-generation artificial intelligence systems. Phononic devices─using heat current to encode and process information─is one of the solutions to neuromorphic computing. In this work, we backmap an artificial neural network (ANN) into a PNN simulation model using polymer networked nanoparticles (PNNPs). Our atomistic simulation results demonstrate that the polymer-linked nanoparticle networks can potentially realize information processing─viz., classification of input temperatures according to the output heat currents. Using high-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and the trust region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) methods, we tune the plasticity of polymer linkers and the temperatures of nanoparticles─28 parameters in total─to optimize the performance of the PNNP machines, which is analogous to tuning of the weights and bias of the corresponding ANNs. After five rounds of high-throughput MD simulations, we demonstrate that the PNNP machine can better label different input temperatures, and thus its performance is improved. We also use a testing data set to verify the heat flow outputs from the top five PNNP machines in each round.

papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) in educational technology has opened new opportunities for enhancing constructivist learning, particularly in computer network education. This study aimed to design, develop, and evaluate Comnet-Art, an AI-based AR learning application, to improve students' understanding and constructivist skills in computer networks. The research involved 234 undergraduate students and employed the ADDIE model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) along with expert validation, practicality testing, and effectiveness assessment. Validation results indicated strong content and media validity, with average Aiken's V scores of 0.92 from media experts and 0.89 from material experts, categorized as very valid. Practicality assessments revealed high usability and engagement, with educators reporting an average practicality score of 91.85% and students 90.71%. Effectiveness evaluation using pre-test and post-test comparisons demonstrated substantial learning gains, with the mean score increasing from 68.21 to 86.47 and a relative improvement of 26.76%, confirming the application's effectiveness in fostering engagement, collaboration, problem-solving, and constructivist learning outcomes. These findings highlight that Comnet-Art successfully integrates AI-driven interactivity and AR visualization to support active learning, improve conceptual understanding, and enhance higher-order cognitive skills. This study provides strong evidence that emerging technologies such as AI and AR can be effectively leveraged to transform engineering education and promote constructivist learning.

papers.title: Learning from Mistakes: Effectiveness of Error Embedded Education in Teaching Osteological Reasoning to First Year MBBS Students
papers.abstract: Background: Osteology classes provide students with the structural framework required for understanding normal anatomical relationships and subsequent clinical application. Despite repeated exposure to bones and anatomical specimens, students continue to make identification and relational errors. Conventional practical teaching emphasizes the recognition of correctly labeled structures, which may provide limited opportunities for students to actively identify, question and correct inaccurate interpretations. Error Embedded Education (EEE) is an educational strategy in which plausible anatomical errors are deliberately incorporated into learning materials, requiring learners to detect, classify, explain and correct the error. This approach may transform errors into active learning opportunities. Aim: To evaluate whether an osteology focused Error Embedded Education approach improves osteological reasoning and error detection ability among 1st year MBBS students compared with conventional osteology teaching. Methods: A prospective, randomized, controlled educational intervention was conducted among 83 1st year MBBS students. Participants were allocated to an Error Embedded Education group (EEE; n=42) and a conventional teaching control group (n=41). Both groups participated in eight weekly 60 minute osteology sessions using the same 10 specimens/images and equivalent instructional time. In the EEE group, realistic structural, positional/relational, variant versus anomaly, and developmental origin errors were deliberately embedded in specimens, images and case-based material. Students were required to identify, classify and correct the errors. The control group received the same specimens/images with correct conventional labeling. The primary outcome was the post module Osteological Reasoning Score (ORS). Secondary outcomes included Error Detection Sensitivity (EDS), 8 week retention of osteological reasoning, cognitive load and identification confidence. Between groups comparisons were performed using independent-samples t-tests, with ANCOVA used as a confirmatory analysis for the primary outcome. Effect sizes were expressed as Cohen's d, and Pearson correlation coefficients were used to explore relationships between selected outcomes. Results: The two groups were comparable at baseline with respect to age, sex, baseline osteological reasoning scores and previous osteology practical exposure. The mean post module ORS was significantly higher in the EEE group than in the control group (78.9 ± 7.6 vs. 70.2 ± 8.8; t=4.83, df=81; p<0.001; Cohen's d=1.06). Error detection sensitivity was also substantially higher among students receiving EEE (71.4 ± 11.2 vs. 52.7 ± 13.6; t=6.84, df=81; p<0.001; Cohen's d=1.50). At eight-week follow-up, the EEE group retained higher osteological reasoning scores than the control group (75.1 ± 8.0 vs. 64.3 ± 9.1; t=5.75, df=81; p<0.001; Cohen's d=1.26). Cognitive load was greater in the EEE group (58.3 ± 12.1 vs. 47.6 ± 11.4; Cohen's d=0.91), suggesting increased cognitive engagement during the intervention. Identification confidence was modestly but significantly higher in the EEE group (3.9 ± 0.6 vs. 3.6 ± 0.7; p=0.039; Cohen's d=0.46). Error detection performance varied according to error type: structural misidentification 82%, positional/relational 74%, variant versus anomaly 68%, and developmental origin errors 59%. Within the EEE group, in-module error-catching performance was positively correlated with post module ORS (r=0.52, p<0.001), whereas cognitive load was not significantly associated with post module ORS (r=0.11, p=0.47). Conclusion: Embedding realistic anatomical errors into osteology teaching significantly improved osteological reasoning, error-detection sensitivity and retention among first-year MBBS students compared with conventional correctly labeled teaching. Although EEE imposed greater cognitive demand, this additional effort was not associated with poorer learning outcomes and may represent productive cognitive engagement. Deliberate exposure to plausible errors, followed by explanation and correction, may therefore provide a useful educational strategy for developing more flexible and reflective anatomical reasoning. Keywords: Error Embedded Education, Osteology, Medical Education; Cognitive conflict, Anatomical Reasoning

papers.title: Amelogenesis Imperfecta as an Emerging Molecular Model for Enamel Biomineralization and Its Implications for Precision Dentistry and Craniofacial Research
papers.abstract: Background: Amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) has recently been realized as not only an inherited enamel anomaly, but also a genetically heterogeneous developmental disorder and a compelling model for the study of enamel biomineralization and craniofacial development. Methods: This review is a narrative synthesis of the state of the art of AI genetics, genotype–phenotype relationships, ameloblast biology, enamel biomineralization, molecular diagnosis and new approaches to regeneration by biomimetic nanomaterials, stem cell engineering, use of organoids, 3D bioprinting, and gene editing. Results: Pathogenic variants of enamel matrix proteins, proteolytic enzymes, ion transport, intracellular trafficking, and signaling between cells and the matrix provide insights into different molecular mechanisms underlying hypoplastic, hypomineralized (hypomaturation), and hypomineralized (hypocalcified) disease. The incorporation of new techniques, such as next-generation sequencing, functional genomics, multi-omics, and computational methods is changing the paradigm of AI from phenotype-based classification to one of molecularly stratified and personalized diagnosis. At the same time, emerging experimental approaches—including biomimetic mineralization, engineered ameloblast-like cells, organoid systems, and genome-editing technologies—provide promising platforms for investigating enamel regeneration, although their clinical applicability remains to be established. Conclusions: AI provides a valuable mechanistic framework for advancing research toward patient-specific, biologically informed approaches in developmental biology, precision dentistry, and regenerative craniofacial medicine; however, regenerative interventions remain investigational and require substantial preclinical validation before potential clinical translation.

papers.title: Predicting the Water Retention Behavior of Biochar-Amended Soils: A Comparative Study of Six Machine Learning Approaches
papers.abstract: The soil-water retention curve (SWRC) is a key indicator characterizing soil water retention capacity. Biochar incorporation can affect the SWRC by altering soil pore structure and physicochemical properties. The SWRC of biochar-amended soils is influenced by both soil- and biochar-related factors. To address the time-consuming and labor-intensive nature of conventional SWRC measurement methods, this study employed six machine learning models, Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Categorical Gradient Boosting (CatBoost), Light Gradient Boosting (LightGBM), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN), to predict the SWRC of biochar-amended soils based on a constructed dataset. Feature importance analysis and partial dependence analysis were also conducted to identify key variables and reveal their influence patterns. The results indicated that gradient boosting tree models, XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM, achieved the highest accuracy, with R2 = 0.85–0.89 on the inner-test set and R2 = 0.61–0.64 on the held-out source, demonstrating their advantage in modeling complex nonlinear relationships. Suction was the variable most strongly associated with volumetric water content, while soil particle-size distribution and particle packing density also played important roles. Among biochar-related parameters, ash content showed higher importance than carbon content and pH. The model-derived response of volumetric water content to ash content was non-uniform: limited at low levels, increasing after reaching a certain range, and stabilizing at high levels. In contrast, carbon content and pH had relatively weak marginal effects. A staged hyperparameter optimization strategy combining random search and Bayesian optimization was then applied to optimize the XGBoost model, yielding accuracy comparable to grid search while substantially reducing the training time. Based on the optimized XGBoost model, a prediction platform for the SWRC of biochar-amended soils was developed, enabling volumetric water content prediction, SWRC generation, and van Genuchten (VG) model fitting. This study provides a data-driven approach and a prototype tool for rapid, preliminary SWRC estimation for biochar-amended soils, thereby facilitating the application of biochar in engineering practice.

papers.title: Active Learning: A Strategy to Improve the Quality of Mathematics Learning
papers.abstract: Active learning is often associated with increased student participation, yet its contribution to mathematics learning quality depends on whether participation generates substantive mathematical thinking. This conceptual review develops an integrative framework explaining how active learning can support higher-quality mathematics learning. Relevant literature on active learning, mathematical activities, student engagement, teacher facilitation, and mathematics learning quality was synthesized to identify their conceptual relationships. The synthesis conceptualizes active learning as a pedagogical orientation enacted through purposeful mathematical activities involving problem solving, representation, reasoning, communication, and reflection. Student engagement functions as the core mechanism through which these activities become meaningful learning experiences, while teacher facilitation operates as a cross-cutting condition that designs, supports, monitors, and adapts learning processes. Mathematics learning quality is conceptualized as an emergent consequence reflected in deeper understanding, mathematical reasoning, problem solving, communication, representation, and meaningful application of knowledge. The resulting framework integrates five interrelated components and five conceptual propositions. Rather than proposing a fixed causal sequence, it represents a dynamic pedagogical system in which purposeful activity, sustained engagement, and responsive facilitation interact to create conditions for meaningful mathematical learning. The framework offers a conceptual basis for designing active mathematics learning and guiding future empirical investigation.

papers.title: AI-Guided Clinical Image Interpretation System for Precision Treatment Planning
papers.abstract: Radiological examinations increasingly leverage artificial intelligence to enhance diagnostic performance by compensating for expertise shortages, particularly in specialized interpretation. Despite academic AI models achieving compelling accuracy, adoption remains low. An objective, evidence-based examination of AI-guided clinical image interpretation seeks to expose the underlying reasons. The primary challenge lies not in accuracy but in fully automated analysis, especially for multimodal and multidimensional datasets. Introduction of uncertainty measures, image explainability, and real-world data reduce recognition to a decisive-supporting role— helping radiologists to detect previously unnoticed abnormalities—or even to precautionary analysis. Patients requesting precision medicine and therapy planning—and those at high risk of neglected pathology—stand to gain the greatest benefit. Relevant AI architecture considers imaging cues suitable for precision medicine or requiring additional methods to obtain interpretable images. Successful performance testing against an external, hidden reference dataset promotes vital user trust. Machine learning achieves best results where all potentially pathological abnormalities are identified and their presence virtually guaranteed, as in multi-class recognition. Data scarcity, however, impedes clinically relevant solutions. Explainability, essential for medical applications and clinical acceptance, extends simply beyond clinical decision support to provide saliency maps and, better still, clinically meaningful image regions or qualities. Attention maps may even bring a form of rule-based reasoning within reach. Clinical integration that reproduces the technical conditions under which model diagnostic measures are calculated raises the challenge of uncertainty quantification—a necessary condition for clinical decision support. Convolutional neural networks trained for photo-quality classification, par excellence supervised image quality assessment, provide the basic cues for uncertainty quantification. Imaging acquisition, modality, and systems are also defined in terms of current PACS/EPIC systems. PE, pre-symptomatic examination or precautionary examination, is defined as a patientuser group prepared to cover the cost of an examination with lower diagnostic accuracy and a high level of uncertainty

papers.title: Hardware-in-the-loop validation of an MPC architecture for real-time equilibrium control of tokamak plasmas at RFX-mod2
papers.abstract: This work deals with the real-time implementation of an equilibrium control system based on Model Predictive Control (MPC) for tokamak plasma operation at RFX-mod2. Such an architecture has been shown to address the challenging asymmetric constraints imposed by the one-quadrant power converters supplying the poloidal field coils at RFX-mod2. However, being based on the solution of constrained optimization problems, the real-time performance of such a control approach must be carefully assessed. To this end, a sensitivity study on the MPC parameters that aims at simplifying the optimization problem to be solved in real-time, while guaranteeing the control performance, is first presented. Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulations are then performed to assess the real-time performance of the controller. Different off-the-shelf solvers are considered when automatically generating the real-time code starting from the Simulink model. The HIL simulations reveal that the choice of the solver has an impact on the execution time, and may make the real-time implementation infeasible for the chosen optimization problem.

papers.title: A defect and multi-physics informed neural network for fatigue life prediction in friction stir welded additive manufacturing AlSi7Mg
papers.abstract: Additively manufactured aluminium alloys joined by friction stir welding exhibit great potential for large-scale structural applications, yet their fatigue life prediction remains challenging due to the complex influence of internal defects and process-induced microstructural heterogeneity. To address this issue, a defect-based, physics-informed neural network framework was proposed for fatigue life prediction of additively manufactured AlSi7Mg friction stir welded joints. A multi-route physics-informed modeling strategy is introduced, incorporating physical prior knowledge through feature engineering, loss function design, and adaptive feature weighting. Four data augmentation methods are employed to enhance data diversity and model robustness, and the results show that among these approaches, Precise Physics Law (PPL) yields the best overall performance. The proposed Defect and Multi-Physics Coupled Informed Neural Network (DM-PINN) dynamically adjusts the weights of physical loss terms based on defect and multi-physics features, achieving a better balance between data-driven learning and physical consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that the DM-PINN model outperforms both conventional artificial neural networks and standard physics-informed neural networks in terms of prediction accuracy, generalization capability, and physical interpretability. The model successfully predicts conditional fatigue limits under different processing conditions with errors below 15%, providing a reliable tool for fatigue life assessment and process optimization of defect-sensitive additive manufacturing components.

papers.title: Engineering Biohybrid Mycelium Fibers through Hierarchical Structuring and Biomineralization
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Engineered living materials (ELMs) that utilize fungal cells have emerged as a class of functional materials, owing to their ability to self‐assemble, adapt, and regenerate. Filamentous fungi growth promotes the formation of a network of interwoven threads, or mycelia, that is of rising interest as a sustainable and versatile material; however, broader application is constrained by comparatively lower strength than synthetic or natural materials. In order to develop mechanical strength, strategies from nature, such as structural hierarchy and mineralization, are leveraged in the material design. In this study, a bioink composed of alginate and a modified strain of the filamentous fungus Aspergillus niger capable of silica mineralization is extruded to create fibers of interconnected mycelium. After fiber incubation, fungal cells exhibit radial hyphal growth extending from the core fiber, which can be tuned by capillary force alignment. Mineralization demonstrates approximately double the stiffness and strength of dried mycelium fibers. Further, twisted and braided fibers exhibit a two‐ to three‐fold increase in elongation at break compared to single fibers. The results show that mycelium morphology and mechanical properties can be tuned through mineralization, growth conditions, and processing.

papers.title: Development and evaluation of a 3D augmented reality application for respiratory anatomy education
papers.abstract: Respiratory anatomy presents substantial learning challenges due to its complex three-dimensional (3D) spatial organization and dynamic functional relationships. Traditional two-dimensional instructional resources, including textbooks and static images, may limit students’ spatial understanding and integration of anatomical knowledge. Augmented reality (AR) technology provides interactive and immersive visualization that may enhance spatial cognition and active learning. This study aimed to develop a respiratory anatomy application incorporating 3D visualization and augmented reality, and to evaluate its content alignment, short-term within-group knowledge-score change and learner-reported experiences in a classroom setting of health science students. A quasi-experimental pre–post study was conducted among 80 first-year physiotherapy students at Srinakharinwirot University, Thailand. The 3D AR application was developed based on defined respiratory anatomy learning objectives and incorporated interactive 3D visualization, layered anatomical structures, and real-time AR manipulation. The application content validity was evaluated using the Item–Objective Congruence (IOC) index by three experts in the content of the application. Two additional experts in the content of the satisfaction and engagement questionnaires. Thus, five experts contributed across these evaluation roles. Respiratory anatomy knowledge was assessed on a 0–10 scale using pre- and post-intervention multiple-choice tests that underwent expert review for content relevance and item–objective alignment using the IOC index. Student engagement and satisfaction were measured the 1–5 range by using structured Likert-scale questionnaires. Descriptive statistics were calculated for all variables. Differences between pre- and post-test scores were analyzed using the Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank test. The application demonstrated high item–objective alignment, with IOC values ranging from 0.90 to 1.00 across the evaluated application components. Students reported high levels of engagement (4.08 ± 0.69) and satisfaction (4.14 ± 0.82). Post-test knowledge scores were higher than pre-test scores after the seven-day period of application use alongside usual learning activities ( p < 0.001). These findings describe within-group changes and learner-reported experiences in this single-group classroom evaluation. In this one-group pre-test/post-test study, students demonstrated higher respiratory anatomy knowledge scores at post-test than at baseline following a seven-day period of application use alongside usual learning activities, together with positive engagement and satisfaction ratings. These findings support further evaluation of the application as a supplementary learning resource for respiratory anatomy education; however, the observed changes cannot be attributed specifically to the application because the study did not include a control group. Controlled studies are required to determine its educational effectiveness.

papers.title: Pool boiling performance of gyroid-structured surfaces subject to R-1233zd(E) refrigerant
papers.abstract: This experimental study investigates the pool boiling heat transfer performance of the low-GWP refrigerant R-1233zd(E) on additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid lattice surfaces. Two gyroid configurations, with unit cell sizes of 1 mm (GL-1) and 1.2 mm (GL-1.2), were examined and compared with a well-polished copper surface having an average roughness of 0.025 μm. Experiments were conducted at saturation pressures of 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 bar under both increasing and decreasing heat flux conditions. The results show that gyroid lattice structures significantly enhance pool boiling heat transfer by improving liquid replenishment, separating vapor and liquid pathways, delaying lateral bubble coalescence, and promoting bubble detachment from the heated surface. At low heat flux under increasing heat flux conditions and 1.5 bar saturation pressure, GL-1 and GL-1.2 achieved HTC enhancements of approximately 582% and 183%, respectively, compared with the smooth surface. Under decreasing heat flux conditions at the highest heat flux and the same pressure, the corresponding HTC enhancements were 105% and 112%. The reason for this improvement lies not only in the lattice-structure-enhanced surface but also in the fabrication process. The study also revealed different boiling hysteresis behavior between smooth and gyroid surfaces. For the smooth surface, HTC was higher during decreasing heat flux operation, whereas the gyroid surfaces showed better performance during increasing heat flux operation. Considering the confinement effect, and area-related efficiency the hystersis phenomena was investigated. As the saturation pressure increased, the difference between increasing and decreasing heat flux conditions decreased, indicating suppression of boiling hysteresis. At the highest tested heat flux of approximately 215 kW·m −2 and 2.5 bar, GL-1 and GL-1.2 achieved maximum HTC enhancements of 85% and 101%, respectively.

papers.title: Physics-informed deep learning modelling of tuberculosis dynamics with waning immunity in diabetic populations: evidence from Saudi Arabia
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) and diabetes mellitus (DM) pose a growing public health challenge in Saudi Arabia, where diabetes-induced immune dysfunction increases TB susceptibility and post-treatment relapse. This study develops a four-compartment TB-DM mathematical model with a saturating incidence function to capture transmission dynamics under high infectious pressure and waning immunity. A Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework is proposed for parameter estimation by integrating observational data with the governing nonlinear dynamical system, enabling biologically consistent and data-efficient learning. The basic reproduction number is derived using the next-generation matrix approach, a closed-form endemic equilibrium is obtained, and local stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibria is established. The PINN accurately recovers model parameters and demonstrates strong predictive performance using synthetic and Saudi tuberculosis surveillance data, including a direct, reproducible comparison against a classical least-squares baseline and a standard, non-physics-informed neural network. Sensitivity and intervention analyses identify transmission intensity, treatment-related recovery, early case detection, and integrated diabetes management as the key levers for reducing TB burden, providing a data-driven framework to support evidence-based TB-DM control policy in Saudi Arabia.

papers.title: FB-PINN: A Fischer-Burmeister-enhanced physics-informed neural network for phreatic line prediction in saturated-unsaturated seepage flow
papers.abstract: Accurate phreatic line prediction is essential for seepage analysis in earth dams, yet traditional mesh-based methods require costly iterative procedures. Existing physics-informed neural network (PINN) approaches typically model only the saturated zone, neglecting the influence of the unsaturated zone. This study develops the FB-PINN, a novel mesh-free neural solver integrating the smoothed Fischer-Burmeister (FB) function into the PINN for steady-state saturated–unsaturated seepage with an unknown seepage face. The seepage face gives rise to a Signorini-type nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP), which the smoothed FB function reformulates as a single smooth equality constraint, eliminating the ill-conditioned loss landscape and gradient oscillation inherent in conventional separate-penalty formulations. Built upon a mixed-form Richards equation and a trunk-branch architecture, FB-PINN simultaneously predicts pressure head, water content, and phreatic line location with high accuracy. The framework is validated across varying water levels, diverse dam geometries, stratified anisotropic materials, and zoned dams with clay cores. A localized numerical cut-off is also introduced to alleviate the strong near-saturation VG nonlinearity in the low-n regime. Following validation of the core formulation, FB-PINN is further extended to support rapid multi-condition seepage prediction through a parameterized surrogate and sparse-observation-based identification of van Genuchten parameters.

papers.title: Seismic Overthrust Fault Detection via Weakly Supervised Active Learning
papers.abstract: Complex overthrust faults in deep seismic data often show weak boundaries and discontinuous spatial extensions. Under sparse annotation, three problems arise: weak-boundary recognition, insufficient three-dimensional connectivity supervision, and uncontrolled pseudo-label propagation. This study proposes a weakly supervised active learning framework with three modules. FG-ResACE U-Net is a two-dimensional segmentation network that outputs section-wise probability maps from amplitude, gradient, and continuity inputs, with wavelet gating, Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP), and attention. Slice predictions are stacked into a three-dimensional probability volume; Top-K windows are selected from this reconstructed volume, not from a three-dimensional CNN, where K=0.02 means the top 2% of candidate windows. Geological-topology active learning ranks windows by prediction entropy, connectivity defects, and strike-direction deviation. Corridor-constrained Mean Teacher accepts positive pseudo-labels only at the intersection of expert candidate corridors and high-confidence teacher predictions. On synthetic overthrust models and Keshen three-dimensional seismic data, the complete framework, under the evaluated settings, shows more continuous main-fault responses and fewer fence-like fragments than the reported architectural variants.

papers.abstract: Abstract Work zones and off-ramp queue spillback are two major bottlenecks on expressways in developed urban areas. However, to our best knowledge, few studies have addressed these two types of bottlenecks simultaneously in expressway traffic control. This paper proposes a coordinated ramp metering and variable speed limit strategy to jointly mitigate work zone congestion and off-ramp queue spillover. A model predictive control framework, consisting of a traffic evolution module and an optimization module, is developed to update optimal control actions in a rolling-horizon manner. The traffic evolution module captures fixed lane drops caused by work zones and predicts dynamic lane drops induced by off-ramp queue spillback. The optimization module incorporates on- and off-ramp storage capacity constraints and designs a hierarchical penalty structure to proactively suppress queue spillover risks. A case study based on a congested urban expressway located in the central urban area of Shanghai is conducted to evaluate the proposed strategy. Results show that the proposed approach effectively mitigates work zone congestion and prevents on-ramp and off-ramp queue spillover. Compared with the no-control scenario, a 23.4% reduction in total time spent is achieved, outperforming traditional coordinated control strategies that neglect off-ramp queue dynamics.

papers.title: West Nile virus reaction–diffusion dynamics on higher-order directed network
papers.abstract: West Nile virus (WNv) has a unique mosquito–bird–mosquito diffusion cycle, so the common compartment model cannot describe its complex spatial spread process. This study generalizes a reaction–diffusion system on continuous space to a complex directed network with a nonlinear diffusion function. By incorporating the Logistic growth of mosquitoes, a three-variable reaction–diffusion system is established. We deduce the basic reproduction number R 0 and Turing instability conditions, and prove that nonlinear diffusion can induce spatial patterns. A periodic diffusion coefficient can also result in patterns, as discussed via Floquet theory. Using optimal control, the optimization problem and parameter identification are derived. Numerical simulations verify the theoretical conclusions, and we further use a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to predict the evolutionary trend based on real data from New Jersey, incorporating temperature into the time-varying transmission rate.

papers.title: Dual-Timescale Robust Rolling Optimal Scheduling of Microgrid Considering Regulation Priority
papers.abstract: To address the power balance and economic operation issues of microgrids with high-penetration renewable energy, this paper explores the synergistic regulation potential of combined heat and power, carbon capture, and power-to-gas, and proposes a multi-timescale robust scheduling method incorporating regulation priorities. First, a grid-connected microgrid model coupling combined heat and power, power-to-gas, and carbon capture is constructed, and a “day-ahead and intra-day” dual-timescale rolling optimization framework is designed. The day-ahead stage coordinates equipment output base values at hourly intervals to minimize total costs, while the intra-day stage employs an affinely adjustable robust model predictive control for rolling corrections at 5 min intervals. Second, a marginal-cost-based power priority coordination strategy is proposed, which defines an explicit regulation sequence for power-to-gas, micro gas turbines, grid electricity purchases, and combined heat and power. Additionally, an adaptive state of charge penalty mechanism for the energy storage system is designed. Finally, the case study results demonstrate that the proposed priority strategy allocates power imbalances in ascending cost order, ensuring both economic viability and low carbon emissions. Meanwhile, the storage state of charge penalty mechanism effectively enhances battery safety and lifespan, achieving multi-objective collaborative optimization.

papers.title: Machine Learning-assisted Antenna Design and Optimization: A Comprehensive Review of Surrogate Modeling, Active Learning, and Intelligent Optimization
papers.abstract: The rapid development of wireless communication systems has created an increasing demand for compact, broadband, high-performance, and application-specific antennas. Conventional antenna design approaches generally rely on analytical formulations, empirical relationships, parameter sweeps, and repeated full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, which become computationally expensive as the number of design variables increases. To address these challenges, metaheuristic optimisation techniques such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) have been widely investigated for exploring complex antenna design spaces. More recently, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches have been introduced for antenna performance prediction, inverse design, and surrogate-assisted optimisation. These approaches can reduce the computational burden associated with repeated EM simulations; however, their effectiveness often depends on sufficiently large and representative simulation datasets. Hybrid ML–metaheuristic approaches further improve the optimisation process by combining predictive models with intelligent search algorithms, while Active Learning enables the selective acquisition of informative simulation samples. This review presents the evolution of computational antenna design from conventional and metaheuristic approaches to ML-based, hybrid, and Active Learning-driven methodologies. The reviewed studies are critically examined with respect to their design strategies, optimisation techniques, simulation requirements, data dependence, and computational efficiency. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of surrogate modelling and adaptive sample selection in reducing expensive full-wave simulations. The review identifies the limitations of existing approaches and highlights the need for autonomous, data-efficient, and simulation-efficient frameworks for high-dimensional microstrip antenna optimisation.

papers.title: A Classroom Intervention Study to Assess the Potential of a 360-Degree Virtual Reality Learning Environment to Enhance Conceptual Understanding and Engagement in Physics
papers.abstract: Abstract The use of individual student laptops and tablets in K-12 classrooms enables large-scale implementation of innovative learning technologies. Theories of multimedia and immersive learning suggest that immersive features can influence cognitive and affective learning processes. Therefore, 360-degree virtual reality learning environments (VRLEs) represent a promising area for further investigation. This study compares an interactive desktop-based low-immersive 360-degree VRLE with a traditional paper-and-pencil approach to investigate effects on students’ conceptual understanding of Galilean transformations of uniform motion in position-time graphs and on student engagement. Both conditions worked with multiple representations within a Predict-Observe-Explain framework to support active learning. A total of 313 students (176 female, 137 male) from the advanced track of upper secondary school participated in the pre-post classroom study. Conceptual understanding was assessed using the Inventory for Galilean Transformation of Uniform Motion in Position-Time Graphs. Students in both conditions improved their understanding, but no significant difference between conditions was observed. However, students using the VRLE reported a stronger inclination to perform well. These findings suggest that 360-degree VRLEs may support certain aspects of self-reported student engagement related to effort, but further research is needed to better understand how learning outcomes can be improved.

papers.title: SIF-Constrained Optimization of SCOPE Vegetation Parameters for Gross Primary Productivity Estimation
papers.abstract: Solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) provides a new pathway for the accurate estimation of gross primary productivity (GPP) by directly probing vegetation photosynthetic functioning, but mechanistic estimation is still constrained by the difficulty of obtaining the seasonal dynamics of key physiological parameters. Using maize, a representative C4 crop, as an experimental case, this study integrated long-term tower-based SIF observations with the SCOPE model to propose a cross-variable constraint strategy, in which key vegetation parameters were optimized against in situ SIF observations and independently validated against eddy covariance-derived GPP. Specifically, key sensitive parameters were first identified via Sobol global sensitivity analysis. A double-baseline asymmetric Gaussian phenology model was then constructed to characterize the seasonal dynamics of Vcmax, while Cab was derived from Vcmax using a smoothed piecewise-linear empirical relationship. A two-stage Bayesian optimization scheme was applied to optimize the parameters, which were subsequently used to run the SCOPE model and reconstruct continuous SIF and GPP time series. The results showed that the estimated daily SIF and GPP agreed well with ground observations, yielding R2 values of 0.86 and 0.74, respectively. Furthermore, the upscaled results correlated strongly with satellite products (MODIS: R = 0.94, R2 = −2.69; PML: R = 0.95, R2 = 0.81). This study demonstrates the feasibility of using SIF observations to constrain SCOPE vegetation parameters for improved GPP estimation, providing a parameterization basis and methodological support for mechanistic remote sensing monitoring of vegetation productivity.

papers.title: Material-Resolved Thermal Boundary Constraints for PINN-Based Urban Micro-Meteorology
papers.abstract: Urban micro-meteorological models often omit building surfaces’ evening heat release. We derive physics-informed thermal boundary constraints from the Surface Energy Balance equation, supplied to a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) through an Urban Thermal-Geometric Database and a Force-Restore model. A 2D heated cavity benchmark at Ra=104, verified against an independent finite-volume reference, reduces interior temperature MAE by 56%, wall-temperature MAE by 97.5% and Nusselt error by 74% across five seeds, at a 16% horizontal-velocity cost, worse in all five. In the open-roof canyon, a five-seed PINN feasibility comparison shows material-resolved wall temperatures reduce blind temperature MAE from 0.00830±0.00050 to 0.00368±0.00058, with much lower matched heat-flux errors than an equivalent-memory homogeneous control and velocity within seed scatter. Seven independent quasi-steady snapshots follow. At 14:00, material resolution raises street-surface heat transfer by 61% while corridor-band velocity variability remains comparable, indicating redistribution rather than amplification. At 18:00 the material-resolved case retains an order-of-magnitude larger σv (0.61 vs. 0.06); at 20:00 it reverses the street-surface heat-flux direction while the mean-temperature case approaches neutrality. It is a constructed near-zero-forcing baseline; ratios to it are not interpreted. The reversal is robust in sign but not in magnitude under slab-model and ±1 K facade-contrast perturbations.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence across the continuum of care for the aging musculoskeletal patient: From longitudinal phenotyping to personalized surgery and recovery monitoring
papers.abstract: Abstract Musculoskeletal care is being reshaped by population aging, multimorbidity, frailty, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, polypharmacy and increasing vulnerability to postoperative loss of independence. Artificial intelligence (AI) has entered orthopaedic research, but its clinical translation remains constrained. Many models address isolated diagnostic, imaging or short‐term prediction tasks rather than the longitudinal care trajectories that determine outcomes in older musculoskeletal patients. The central limitation is therefore not simply whether older adults are represented in datasets, but whether AI systems are valid across the continuum of geriatric orthopaedic care. This review argues for a transition from task‐specific orthopaedic AI toward continuum‐of‐care AI for the aging musculoskeletal patient. Upstream, radiomics, longitudinal osteoarthritis phenotyping, opportunistic computed tomography (CT)‐based skeletal assessment and AI‐augmented dual‐energy X‐ray absorptiometry (DXA) modelling may improve prediction of disease progression, fracture risk, treatment failure and surgical timing. At the point of intervention, AI‐assisted arthroplasty planning may help move total knee arthroplasty from generic alignment targets toward phenotype‐specific reconstruction strategies that account for constitutional alignment, bone morphology, ligament envelope, neuromuscular control, frailty and functional reserve. Perioperatively, automated frailty and sarcopenia phenotyping, wearable gait analysis and multimodal temporal models integrating imaging, electronic health records, laboratory data, medications, patient‐reported outcomes and wearable signals may support dynamic risk prediction. After discharge, continuous monitoring of mobility, sleep, pain trajectories, wound‐related symptoms and rehabilitation adherence may help close the high‐risk surveillance gap during the 90‐day postoperative episode. However, clinical adoption requires more than high discrimination. Explainable AI should be understood as one component of a broader trust framework that also includes calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision‐curve analysis, external and prospective validation, workflow integration, post‐deployment monitoring and accountability. The future of orthopaedic AI is not simply better diagnosis or more precise surgery, but longitudinal, multimodal support across the full care continuum: predicting progression, selecting treatment, personalizing surgery, optimizing perioperative care, monitoring recovery and preserving mobility and independence. Level of Evidence Level IV.

papers.title: Textual World Models for Agent Security: Modelling the Internal State of an LLM Agent from Text Alone
papers.abstract: An AI agent chooses its own path to reach an objective, so its security and compliance depend on its internal state, not only on its inputs and outputs. We ask whether the activations of the agent's large language model (LLM), produced when it reads the context, are a sufficient observation of this state to build a model of it, without any access to the agent's tools or design. We test sufficiency by prediction: a world model built on these activations should predict the agent's next step. Because the agent's LLM is usually not accessible, a small witness LLM reads the same context. On 22 agents, the resulting model predicts that the next answer will carry out a prompt-injection attack with an AUROC of 0.93, and identifies the conversation in which the agent will give in for 63 % of pairs that a lookup table cannot separate. The observation is partial, as expected: nothing predicts an attack before it enters the context, because that part of the state is held by the tools.
