papers.title: Machine learning–driven strength prediction and optimal waste glass powder dosage for concrete exposed to high temperatures
papers.abstract: This study explores the synergistic effects of the addition of waste glass powder (WGP) and elevated temperatures on the mechanical behavior of concrete, and proposes a machine-learning-based framework for mixture design optimization. Six concrete mixtures containing 0–50% WGP were tested for compressive, flexural, and splitting tensile strengths over the temperature range 24–600 °C, and the results consistently showed an optimal WGP dosage of 10–20% at room temperature and a pronounced degradation in these strengths above 400 °C. To model the strength evolution across the entire WGP-temperature space, a physics-aware data augmentation method and a multi-output Random Forest surrogate model are developed and validated using mixture-wise three-fold cross-validation, parity plots, Y-randomization tests, SHAP-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification. The validated surrogate is then combined with NSGA-II to determine WGP dosages that simultaneously maximize room-temperature strength, high-temperature residual capacity, and material efficiency. Both prospective within-domain experimental validation showed close agreement between the surrogate predictions and independently measured responses. Contour maps and optimization results also consistently show that the 10–20% WGP dosage offers the best trade-off between initial strength and thermal resilience. The results demonstrate the two-fold role of WGP as a micro-filler in improving ambient performance and as a thermally sensitive phase governing degradation mechanisms at elevated temperatures. Therefore, this work presents a validated ML-based framework and practical design charts for optimizing WGP-modified concrete for fire-exposed or high-temperature applications. SEM analyses of the glass powder-reinforced concrete sample exposed to 600 °C showed an increase in cracks and voids in the microstructure; EDX results indicated Ca enrichment with the dominance of O (51.49%), Ca (20.78%), and Si (8.17%); FT-IR spectrum showed the disappearance of the ~ 3400 and ~ 1650 cm⁻¹ bands and the weakening of the ~ 950–1000 cm⁻¹ band, confirming C–S–H degradation; and XRD analysis revealed a decrease in amorphous humps and the prominence of crystalline peaks, indicating that the structure became more crystalline and brittle at high temperature. TGA results indicated that room-temperature-cured samples exhibited higher mass loss and progressive degradation at low temperatures, whereas samples pre-exposed to 600 °C exhibited reduced mass loss and enhanced thermal stability, owing to prior dehydration and microstructural reorganization.

papers.title: AI-Driven Early Warning Systems for Flash Floods Using Satellite Imagery: A GeoAI-Based Framework for Real-Time Flash Flood Prediction, Risk Reduction and the Future of Intelligent Disaster Management
papers.abstract: Abstract: Flash floods remain among the most destructive and least predictable hydrometeorological hazards, characterized by rapid onset, localized intense precipitation, and minimal warning time. This paper critically examines whether the convergence of satellite Earth Observation (EO), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and hydrometeorological intelligence can transform flashflood early warning from a predominantly reactive, detectionoriented paradigm into a predictive, anticipatory, and progressively autonomous disaster intelligence system. Through an interdisciplinary synthesis of remote sensing science, deep learning architectures, spatiotemporal modelling, and disaster risk reduction, we propose the AISatellite Flash Flood Early Warning Intelligence Framework (AISFFEWI)—a conceptual architecture that integrates multisource satellite data, groundbased observations, physicsinformed AI, uncertainty quantification, impact forecasting, and community feedback. The study distinguishes carefully between flood detection and actionable early warning, and emphasizes that lead time, false alarm mitigation, and explainability are as critical as prediction accuracy. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of satellite data sources, AI model suitability, spatiotemporal deep learning, and the severe challenges posed by class imbalance, nonstationary climate conditions, and limited crossregion model transferability. A dedicated Indiacentric perspective examines Himalayan and urban flash floods, while a futureoriented timeline (2026–2050) explores the gradual emergence of AIenabled digital twin watersheds and autonomous warning agents, always balancing technological promise against scientific caution, ethical accountability, and the imperative of communitycentred response. The paper concludes that while satelliteAI systems hold substantial potential to enhance flashflood warning, they cannot replace hydrological understanding, institutional trust, and the human decisionmaking required to convert a probabilistic hazard forecast into lifesaving action.

The relevance of the study stems from the uncertainty of the actual thermal properties of existing buildings and the operating conditions of their heating and ventilation systems, which may lead to substantial discrepancies between calculated and measured energy consumption. The aim is to develop and validate an integrated approach combining on-site measurements, uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, and model calibration. A simplified hourly resistance–capacitance (RC) model using a 3R1C scheme is proposed for simulating the thermal regime of a typical four-storey educational building in Vinnytsia, Ukraine. The uncertainty of nine input parameters is assessed using the Monte Carlo method, while global sensitivity analysis is performed using Sobol indices. The results indicate that the annual space heating demand ranges from 92 to 137 kWh/m² within the 5–95% uncertainty interval. The infiltration air change rate is identified as the dominant parameter, accounting for 64% of the variance in heating demand. Wall thermal transmittance and the indoor temperature setpoint have substantially smaller effects, whereas solar gains and internal heat gains play an important role in determining overheating conditions. The study demonstrates that simultaneous calibration of all influential parameters against heat meter data may produce physically unrealistic parameter estimates due to the compensation of errors. To overcome this limitation, a two-stage calibration procedure is proposed. First, directly measured parameters, including infiltration, ventilation airflow, and indoor temperature, are fixed in the model. The remaining influential parameters are then adjusted through calibration. In a virtual experiment, this approach reduced the monthly normalized mean bias error (NMBE) from 14.5% to 1.0% and reproduced the wall thermal transmittance with an error of 2.6%. The proposed methodology improves the reliability of building energy simulations and provides a basis for substantiated decisions concerning thermal modernization and the optimization of heating and ventilation systems.

papers.title: Adaptive Inversion of the Curie Isothermal Surface in the Ordos Basin and Surrounding Regions Based on Multiple Constraints and Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: The Curie isothermal surface (CIS), the depth at which crustal rocks reach the Curie temperature of magnetite, provides important information on the thermal state of the crust and, through it, of the lithosphere. Conventional magnetic anomaly spectral methods for CIS inversion commonly rely on manually selected spectral parameters, leading to considerable subjectivity and uncertainty. This study proposes an adaptive CIS inversion method based on multiple geophysical constraints and Bayesian optimization. The method integrates de-fractal spectral analysis with a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) to jointly optimize the fractal index, moving-window size, and spectral fitting ranges for estimating the top and centroid depths of the magnetic layer. Multiple constraints, including heat flow, spatial distribution consistency and effective data coverage, are incorporated into the objective function. Synthetic experiments show that the proposed method improves inversion accuracy, reducing RMSE and MAE by 24.3% and 33.8%, respectively, compared with the conventional fixed-parameter method. Application to the Ordos Basin and surrounding regions reveals CIS depths of 20–40 km, with deeper values in the western and northern parts of the basin interior, and shallower values in the eastern and southern parts of the basin interior and in surrounding tectonic zones. The spatial distribution of the CIS in the study area, together with the crustal structures and the seismicity, helps to clarify the regional thermal state and tectonic evolution.

papers.title: Association of different Factors with Academic Performance Among Optometry Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: Academic performance among optometry students is influenced by multiple educational, institutional, and personal factors. Understanding these determinants is essential for improving educational quality and producing competent eye-care professionals. Limited evidence is available regarding factors affecting academic achievement among optometry students in India, particularly in Maharashtra. Aim of the study to correlate the different factors with academic performance of optometry students. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 461 optometry students enrolled in institutions across the Konkan division of Maharashtra. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing academic resources, learning environment, student capacity to engage with learning, and course workload. Academic performance was categorized as unsatisfactory, fair, good, or excellent. Descriptive statistics and Chisquare tests were used to determine associations between educational determinants and academic performance. Results: The mean age of participants was 21.15 ± 1.82 years, and 74.6% were females. Significant associations were observed between academic performance and all educational determinants studied. Academic resources demonstrated a strong association with academic achievement (χ²=256.2, p<0.0001). Students with higher scores in these domains consistently achieved better academic outcomes. Conclusion: Academic performance among optometry students is significantly influenced by academic resources, learning environment, student engagement, and workload management. Student engagement emerged as the most influential determinant. Strengthening educational infrastructure, promoting active learning, and improving academic support systems may enhance academic outcomes and professional competency among optometry students.

papers.title: An Interdisciplinary Framework for Non-Invasive Aesthetic Support in Post-Orthopedic Recovery
papers.abstract: Purpose: This paper examines how non-invasive aesthetic support procedures can be integrated into postoperative orthopedic recovery pathways. Orthopedic interventions frequently entail extended recovery periods marked by discomfort, temporary body image concerns, localized swelling, and reduced physical confidence. Conventional rehabilitation prioritizes mobility restoration and functional recovery, leaving supportive aesthetic approaches underdeveloped within existing recovery frameworks. Methodology: The study developed a patient-centered conceptual model, the Post-Orthopedic Aesthetic Support Framework, through a structured synthesis of the psychosocial, lymphological, and rehabilitation literature. The model was then illustrated by an observational clinical case of a 63-year-old female patient following total hip arthroplasty, assessed over five weeks with Patient-Reported Outcome Measures. Findings: Two modalities, adaptive pressotherapy and microcurrent stimulation, complement established rehabilitation pathways while maintaining a clear distinction between medical treatment and wellness-oriented support. In the observed case, staged aesthetic support was associated with reduced perceived tissue heaviness, faster subjective resolution of visible hematomas, restored sleep quality, and lower reported anxiety. Improved subjective comfort coincided with higher reported adherence to prescribed physical therapy. Unique contribution to theory, practice and policy: The framework converts fragmented evidence on compression therapy and psychosocial support into a single operational pathway with explicit professional boundaries. It supplies aesthetic centers with a safety-bounded referral protocol and provides orthopedic services with a structured option for managing superficial soft-tissue distress after discharge. The model is conceptual and practice-oriented, and it requires further clinical validation.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Accelerating the discovery of materials with extreme lattice thermal conductivity () is limited by the high cost of first‐principles screening. Here, we develop an LLM‐assisted low‐ discovery workflow, where Bayesian optimization (BO) proposes candidates, an LLM performs evidence‐conditioned re‐ranking, and physics‐based structure generation, stability validation, and calculations serve as the acceptance criteria. This integration enables efficient candidate prioritization while maintaining rigorous physical validation. The workflow identifies dynamically stable Ag‐based chalcogenides, including Ag 3 SbSe 4 , Ag 4 TiSe 4 , and Ag 4 TiTe 4 . Mechanistic analysis reveals that their ultralow originates from strong phonon renormalization and coherence‐dominated heat transport. Ag 3 SbSe 4 is predicted to reach a maximum of 2.94 at 500 K due to its ultralow of 0.11 W . Furthermore, automated high‐throughput screening of ternary compounds containing 14 elements identifies 2742 dynamically stable materials with W . These results demonstrate that evidence‐conditioned LLM re‐ranking effectively enhances BO‐driven, physics‐validated materials discovery.

papers.title: A Novel Perspective on Explainability: Measuring and Tuning XAI Consensus
papers.abstract: Neural networks are commonly regarded as black boxes, necessitating post-hoc Explainable AI (XAI) methods. However, different feature attribution techniques applied to the same model and data often yield divergent explanations, undermining the reliability of any single method. This work proposes a model-centric approach that moves beyond evaluating individual XAI methods, focusing instead on optimizing neural network architectures toward cross-method consensus via surrogate-based multi-objective hyperparameter tuning. Cross-method XAI consensus, defined as the degree to which diverse attribution techniques yield convergent explanations for a given architecture, is formalized as a novel optimization objective. Consensus is operationalized by aggregating local attributions into global feature importance profiles, standardizing them, and quantifying convergence via the Euclidean distance. This score is integrated as a second objective alongside predictive loss into a Kriging-based Bayesian optimization framework using desirability functions. Empirical evaluation across 14 diverse datasets confirms that explicitly tuning for explainability is feasible. The framework reveals a prevalent performance-explainability trade-off in most in-distribution settings, while analysis of tuning trajectories and selected architectures reveals exploitable structure in the hyperparameter-to-consensus landscape. These findings introduce cross-method XAI consensus as a practical, model-level criterion for neural architecture selection and provide a quantitative basis for analyzing the performance-explainability trade-off.

papers.title: Digital Twins and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) in Industry 4.0: Real-Time Synchronization, Multi-Scale Simulation, and Edge-Cloud Architectures
papers.abstract: Abstract—The Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0) has driven the convergence of physical industrial equipment with high-fidelity virtual models, establishing the paradigm of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Digital Twins (DTs). A production-grade Digital Twin is not merely a static 3D computer-aided design (CAD) asset; it represents an active, bidirectional, and temporally coupled virtual entity that continuously synchronizes with its physical counterpart across the entire operational lifecycle. However, realizing closed-loop autonomous control and multi-scale simulation across distributed smart manufacturing systems presents profound systems engineering challenges: achieving deterministic sub-millisecond synchronization over non-deterministic industrial networks, solving non-linear partial differential equations (PDEs) at edge line rates, harmonizing heterogeneous semantic schemas (e.g., Asset Administration Shells, OPC UA), and maintaining verifiable transactional provenance across multi-tiered supply chains. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of real-time Digital Twins for Industry 4.0. We formalize physical-virtual state divergence under stochastic transport delays, establish the mathematical foundations of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) as surrogate PDE solvers for real-time finite element analysis (FEA), and model deterministic Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN, IEEE 802.1Qbv) communication bounds. Furthermore, we construct an empirical industrial testbed consisting of an automated robotic manufacturing cell and high-speed CNC milling apparatus connected via a 5G-TSN converged edge-cloud hierarchy. Our empirical results demonstrate that PINN surrogate models reduce thermomechanical stress simulation latency from 4.2 seconds to 8.6 milliseconds (a 488x speedup) while preserving 98.4% structural accuracy compared to classical ANSYS solvers. Concurrently, TSN time-aware traffic scheduling caps physical-to-virtual state synchronization jitter to under 12.4 microseconds. Finally, we establish open research directions in quantum-accelerated multiscale modeling, autonomous twin co-evolution, and zero-trust asset cybersecurity.

papers.abstract: This article examines the linguacultural representation of education and knowledge in English phraseological units. The study is based on the view that phraseological expressions function not only as stable linguistic combinations but also as carriers of culturally significant meanings, values, and ways of conceptualizing human experience. Drawing on approaches to phraseology, сultural studies, and cognitive linguistics, the research explores how education and knowledge are represented through figurative and conventionalized expressions in English. Particular attention is paid to the phraseological units hit the books, learn the ropes, knowledge is power, and know something inside out. The analysis considers their figurative meanings, conceptual structures, and linguacultural significance. The findings demonstrate that education is commonly represented through the concepts of effort, active learning, experience, and practical competence, while knowledge is conceptualized as a source of power, capability, depth, and mastery. The study shows that English phraseological units provide valuable evidence of culturally established attitudes toward learning and intellectual development. Thus, phraseological analysis can contribute to a deeper understanding of the relationship between language, cognition, and culture.

papers.abstract: Abstract Aims Trochanteric fractures (TF) are among the most frequent fractures and have major impact on the affected patients and the healthcare system. Cephalomedullary nails (CMN) are widely used for these fractures. Complications remain frequent, either due to comorbidities or concerning the implant. The goal of this retrospective, single-centre study was to compare the complication rates of two CMN from one manufacturer. Materials and methods All internal fixations TF performed between 01/2017 and 07/2021 in our institution were analysed retrospectively. Follow-up was at least two years. The CMN were the PFN-A or the TFN-A. Demographic data, all reoperations and revisions were recorded. Reoperations and revisions were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with subgrouping as minor reoperation, minor revision or major revision, including conversion to total hip arthroplasty. Results A total of 492 CMN, used in 475 patients, could be included. Among these, 248 were PFN-A and 244 were TFN-A. The overall reoperation rate was 15%, 12.9% for the PFN-A and 17.2% for the TFN-A, respectively. The TFN-A group had significantly more major revisions (hazard ratio 3.57 (95% confidence interval 1.42–9.94; p = 0.004). No relevant differences were found regarding demographic data or the quality of reduction and internal fixation. Discussion The TFN-A had a significantly higher rate of complications leading to major revision than the former PFN-A. This may have been missed when considering only the reoperation rate for all causes due to a camouflage effect by minor complications.

papers.abstract: The increasing deployment of smart meters and Internet of Things technologies has created a demand for intelligent computational systems capable of jointly forecasting electricity consumption, detecting abnormal behavior, and optimizing load management. This study proposes an integrated artificial intelligence-based framework for automated energy metering and consumption management in smart-grid environments. The framework combines a Long Short-Term Memory network for short-term load forecasting, an autoencoder-based model for anomaly detection, and Model Predictive Control for demand-side optimization. The system architecture includes data acquisition, communication, preprocessing, predictive analytics, anomaly monitoring, and decision-support layers. The primary empirical evaluation used 4,380 measured hourly observations (approximately 6 months) from a single administrative building. A separately flagged synthetic temporal extension was retained only as an auxiliary dataset and was excluded from all primary performance metrics. Across five independent model initializations, the final LSTM achieved a MAPE of 3.423 ± 0.555%, an RMSE of 0.336 ± 0.048 kW, and an R 2 of 0.973 ± 0.007 on the 633-sequence independent measured test subset. The synthetic extension was maintained as a separately identified auxiliary component and was excluded from all primary training, validation, and independent test metrics. Using a validation-selected reconstruction-error threshold, the autoencoder detected 12 of 30 controlled anomalies in the independent test subset, yielding 100.00% precision, 40.00% recall, and an F1-score of 57.14%. Under the same controlled protocol, One-Class SVM achieved higher recall (53.33%) and F1-score (69.57%), indicating that the autoencoder should be interpreted as an architectural component rather than as the best-performing anomaly detector for the present dataset. A historical proof-of-concept MPC simulation, retained for architectural illustration, reported a 15% reduction in simulated peak demand and a 12% reduction in estimated electricity cost; these values are not interpreted as measured outcomes from the administrative-building experiment. Controlled anomaly injection was used to establish reproducible validation and test labels for the anomaly-detection component. The results demonstrate that the joint integration of forecasting, anomaly detection, and predictive control provides a computationally coherent framework for supporting energy-management efficiency, operational reliability, and data-driven decision-making in intelligent energy systems.

papers.title: Intelligence-enabled smart inhalable biomaterials for chronic inflammatory airway diseases: integrating responsive carrier engineering, lung-on-chip validation, and patient-specific pulmonary modeling
papers.abstract: Chronic inflammatory airway diseases, particularly asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), are commonly treated by inhalation, yet the nominal dose placed in an inhaler often differs substantially from the dose that reaches diseased airway regions, crosses mucus, enters target cells, and remains pharmacologically active. Airway narrowing, heterogeneous ventilation, mucus plugging, impaired mucociliary clearance, oxidative and proteolytic stress, epithelial barrier dysfunction, inflammatory-cell diversity, device characteristics, and patient-specific inhalation maneuvers jointly shape therapeutic exposure. Smart inhalable biomaterials can be designed to address some of these barriers by controlling transport, retention, activation, or release, but many systems are still optimized primarily at the nanoparticle level and evaluated in static models that do not capture realistic aerosol performance or patient-specific deposition. This review develops an intelligence-enabled bioengineering framework linking disease-informed material design with machine-learning-assisted formulation optimization, formulation–device–patient coupling, lung-on-chip validation, and patient-specific pulmonary modeling. Within this framework, airway features such as mucus architecture, redox gradients, protease activity, epithelial permeability, immune-cell state, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and regional airflow are considered measurable variables that can inform material design and evaluation. The material platforms considered include mucus-penetrating and mucoadhesive carriers, responsive materials, transformable nano-in-micro systems, polymeric and lipid nanoparticles, biomimetic carriers, extracellular vesicles, and systems for pulmonary delivery of nucleic acids and biologics. Their development is considered alongside structured experimental design, machine learning, active learning, mechanistic aerosol modeling, physics-informed surrogates, multi-objective optimization, and uncertainty analysis. Lung-on-chip systems provide human-relevant settings in which deposited dose, mucus transport, barrier function, immune responses, and repeated-exposure effects can be examined under air–liquid-interface and breathing-like conditions. Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics and reduced-order models can complement these platforms by predicting regional deposition, whereas the term digital twin should be reserved for longitudinally updated, uncertainty-aware models linked to actionable decisions. Together, these approaches support a closed-loop design–delivery–validation strategy in which material performance, aerosol behavior, biological response, and patient-specific deposition are evaluated as connected rather than separate development problems.

papers.title: Strip flatness prediction in cold rolling: a review of models, challenges, and emerging directions
papers.abstract: Abstract Cold rolling is one of the most widely applied metal-forming processes, where strip flatness is a critical quality requirement affecting downstream manufacturability, dimensional accuracy and product performance. Flatness defects arise from non-uniform longitudinal stresses generated through tightly coupled interactions between roll bite mechanics, roll stack deformation, friction and lubrication, material behaviour and post-bite buckling. Although numerous modelling strategies exist, the literature remains fragmented across analytical, numerical, hybrid and data driven approaches, making it difficult to identify the most appropriate tools for prediction and control. This review provides a unified framework for strip flatness prediction in cold rolling, presenting a structured taxonomy of modelling approaches and evaluating their assumptions, predictive capability, computational cost and industrial applicability. Analytical and semi-analytical models are compared with numerical techniques and hybrid coupled formulations. Key transversal components, including constitutive laws, friction and lubrication models and buckling formulations, are examined with respect to their influence on widthwise stress distributions and the formation of flatness defects. Recent developments in physics-based, data driven and hybrid modelling, including digital twins and reduced-order models, are discussed with emphasis on their potential to meet the real-time requirements of advanced flatness-control systems. Major research gaps are identified in mixed-lubrication modelling, advanced constitutive descriptions, transient buckling prediction, standardised validation benchmarks and hybrid physics–data driven modelling to support digital twin deployment. By synthesising current knowledge and highlighting emerging research directions, this review provides guidance for selecting and developing strip modelling strategies capable of supporting high precision crown and flatness control in modern, data-enriched rolling mills.

papers.title: A Fusion State-of-Charge Estimation Framework for Lithium-Ion Batteries of Electric Vehicles Using Enhanced Single Particle Model and CNN-BiLSTM
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is critical for driving range prediction and battery safety in lithium-ion electric vehicles. Purely data-driven methods often lack physical interpretability, whereas electrochemical models are limited by model complexity, parameter identification, and real-time computational burden. This study proposes a physics-guided SOC estimation framework that integrates an enhanced single-particle model (ESPM) with a convolutional bidirectional long short-term memory network (CNN-BiLSTM). The ESPM incorporates electrolyte-phase dynamics and derives electrode utilization variables to describe internal electrochemical states. These physically meaningful variables are combined with measured current, voltage, and temperature as hybrid inputs, while Bayesian optimization is used to tune key hyperparameters. Experiments are performed on A123 lithium iron phosphate cells under FUDS, DST, and US06 profiles from −10 to 40 °C. The proposed framework limits maximum relative SOC errors to 4% under DST and 3% under US06, with maximum RMSE and MAE values of 1.35% and 1.08%. Compared with LSTM, GRU, and CNN-BiLSTM baselines, the framework improves estimation accuracy by 15.16% to 51.06%, demonstrating improved robustness under dynamic and wide-temperature conditions.
